name: Vidago Palace Hotel
insider_take: This Belle Époque masterpiece sits majestically in Portugal's pristine Vidago Natural Park, where royalty once retreated to sip legendary thermal waters.
whats_special: Built in 1910 for Portuguese royalty, this palace hotel features its own natural thermal springs with healing properties known since Roman times. The hotel's championship golf course was designed by Mackenzie Ross, architect of Turnberry's famous Ailsa course. The property spans 100 acres of protected parkland in the UNESCO World Heritage Douro region.
pro_tip: Book the signature thermal spa treatments using the hotel's own mineral-rich spring water - the same waters that attracted European nobility over a century ago.
dont_miss: The original 1910 ballroom with hand-painted ceiling frescoes, and a round of golf on the spectacular 18-hole championship course surrounded by ancient chestnut forests. The nearby Pedras Salgadas Natural Park offers pristine hiking trails and additional therapeutic springs just 10 minutes away.
pros: Historic Belle Époque palace architecture with grand elegance
Natural thermal springs and world-class spa facilities
Championship golf course designed by Mackenzie Ross
Extensive parkland setting in Peneda-Gerês National Park region
cons: Remote location in northern Portugal mountains
Limited dining and entertainment options in surrounding area
